entry.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
entry.summary:
Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive route for disease screening via exhaled breath analysis. However, progress in the field is hindered by the lack of systematic benchmarks that compare machine learning methods under realistic conditions, particularly sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode. Most existing studies rely on small, private datasets with inconsistent protocols, rendering results non-comparable and slowing progress.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State. Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $ρ_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cotΘ_H\sim T^2$.
entry.summary:
Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $ρ_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cotΘ_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #high-energy #combinatorics

entry.title: Dynamics-preserving graph sparsification. Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions.
entry.summary:
Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #complex-systems #combinatorics

entry.title: A Common Exponential Lower Bound for Dantzig and Modified Simplex in Deterministic Discounted Games
entry.summary:
On a family of $N$-state deterministic two-player discounted games, every run that chooses adaptively between Dantzig's rule and modified simplex requires $2^{Ω(N)}$ switches from a specified initial strategy, regardless of tie breaking. More generally, a return-gate construction lets Dantzig reproduce any finite Bland prefix in an undiscounted deterministic Markov decision process with rational rewards whenever every visited policy reaches a common sink from all states. Applied to an acyclic binary counter, deleting the minimizer's return actions preserves every fixed maximizing strategy's value at each original state while reducing Dantzig's switch count from exponential to linear.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #combinatorics
